newsitem.title: USA: Modine FY97 sales hurt by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Modine FY97 sales hurt by strong dollar.

text.p: Modine Manufacturing Co said Thursday the strong U.S. dollar reduced sales by $22 million for its fiscal year 1997 ended March 31.

The company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.54 a share compared with $0.46 a share last year. Sales were $243.34 million, down from $244.17 million last year, and for the fiscal year sales rose one percent to $999.05 million.

"With nearly one-third of Modine's annual sales being in other than U.S. currency, the stronger dollar had a negative translation effect of approximately $22 million on fiscal 1997 consolidated sales, compared with the prior year," the company said. "Excluding the impact of the change in exchange rates, worldwide consolidated sales were up by 3.1 percent."

Modine said its largest sales increase was in the passenger-car and light-truck market, due largely to 12 months of sales from Signet Systems. Sales to customers in the off-highway-equipment market had the next largest increase, but medium- and heavy-truck market sales were down, reflecting the industry's continuing weakness in North America.
Cost of sales fell 1.8 percent in the fiscal year, primarily as a result of lower copper and aluminum prices, the company said.
